message.content:
Context: User reports that the breadcrumb at the top of the InkOS app always shows "Dashboard" — even when on `/clients`, `/artists/[id]`, etc. They want it fully dynamic: show the correct crumb trail on every page, including detail pages with entity names (e.g., "Dashboard > Clients > Jane Doe").

Working directory: `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/InkOS`

Report thoroughly:

1. **Full `lib/breadcrumbs.ts`** — read the WHOLE file. Report every segment label, every special-case branch, and how `getBreadcrumbs(pathname, tab, dynamicLabels)` is structured. Are detail pages handled?

2. **Where breadcrumbs render** — grep `getBreadcrumbs` + `<Breadcrumb` imports. List every call site. Most importantly, find the site in `components/app/sidebar/AppHeader.tsx` — report how pathname is obtained (`usePathname()`?), whether `searchParams` is read, and whether any `dynamicLabels` map is passed.

3. **Why is it stuck on "Dashboard"** — read the relevant lines of AppHeader. Is the breadcrumb hardcoded? Is `usePathname()` returning the wrong value? Is there a fallback that defaults to Dashboard?

4. **Dynamic label collection** — Is there a pattern (context, route-level export, or layout prop) where detail pages can inject a "human readable name" for the dynamic segment (e.g., the client's first+last name)? Or does every detail page need to opt-in manually?

5. **List all current routes** under `app/(app)/` that are missing proper breadcrumb coverage — especially detail routes with dynamic segments like `/clients/[id]`, `/artists/[id]`, `/bookings/[id]`, `/payroll/runs/[id]`, `/flash-events/[id]`, `/guest-artists/[id]`, etc.

6. **Tab-host pages** — the sidebar uses `?tab=xxx` query params for Clients (All/Tags/AI Design/Consent), Artists/Team (Roster/Schedules/...), Inventory (Stock/Ink Registry), Payments (Transactions/Commissions/Payroll), Appointments (All/Today/Waitlist), Marketing (Campaigns/Referrals). Does the breadcrumb currently show the active tab as a crumb?

7. **Settings tree** — `/settings/studio/services`, `/settings/account/profile`, etc. Report what the breadcrumb shows on these routes. Is "Settings > Studio > Services" rendered correctly?

Quote file:line for every finding. Under 600 words. Be thorough — this is for a production-grade fix.

1	/**
2	 * S18 — Breadcrumb builder.
3	 *
4	 * Replaces the legacy `[Studio] > [Location?] > [Page]` pattern in AppHeader
5	 * with a proper `Dashboard > [Section] > [Page/Tab/Entity]` hierarchy driven
6	 * by the current pathname + search params.
7	 *
8	 * Usage:
9	 *   const crumbs = getBreadcrumbs(pathname, searchParams.get('tab'), {})
10	 *
11	 * Detail pages can override a dynamic segment's label (e.g., "[id]" → client
12	 * name) by passing a `dynamicLabels` map keyed by the built-up sub-pathname:
13	 *   getBreadcrumbs('/clients/abc123', null, { '/clients/abc123': 'Jane Doe' })
14	 *   → [Dashboard, Clients, Jane Doe]
15	 */
16	
17	export interface Crumb {
18	  /** Display label. */
19	  label: string
20	  /**
21	   * Optional href. When omitted, the crumb renders as the current-page anchor
22	   * (bold, non-link). The last crumb in a trail should always omit href.
23	   */
24	  href?: string
25	}
26

131	/**
132	 * Produce a breadcrumb trail for the given pathname + tab.
133	 *
134	 * Rules:
135	 *  - Always starts with `Dashboard` (linking to `/dashboard`), except on
136	 *    `/dashboard` itself where Dashboard becomes the current-page crumb.
137	 *  - Each subsequent path segment becomes a crumb. Middle crumbs link to the
138	 *    accumulated sub-pathname; the last crumb omits its href.
139	 *  - Unknown segments fall back to the raw segment text (useful for UUIDs
140	 *    during detail-page navigation — the page itself can override via
141	 *    `dynamicLabels`).
142	 *  - Tab hosts append a third crumb when `?tab=` matches a known tab key.
143	 */
144	export function getBreadcrumbs(
145	  pathname: string,
146	  tab: string | null,
147	  dynamicLabels: Record<string, string> = {},
148	): Crumb[] {
149	  // Normalize: strip trailing slash
150	  const path = pathname === '/' ? '/dashboard' : pathname.replace(/\/$/, '')
151	
152	  // /dashboard is the root — single-crumb, current page
153	  if (path === '/dashboard') {
154	    return [{ label: 'Dashboard' }]
155	  }
156	
157	  // Admin section has its own root (not under Dashboard)
158	  if (path.startsWith('/admin')) {
159	    return buildTrail(path, tab, dynamicLabels, { rootLabel: 'Admin', rootHref: '/admin' })
160	  }
161	
162	  return buildTrail(path, tab, dynamicLabels, { rootLabel: 'Dashboard', rootHref: '/dashboard' })
163	}
164	
165	interface BuildTrailOptions {
166	  rootLabel: string
167	  rootHref: string
168	}
169	
170	function buildTrail(
171	  path: string,
172	  tab: string | null,
173	  dynamicLabels: Record<string, string>,
174	  { rootLabel, rootHref }: BuildTrailOptions,
175	): Crumb[] {
176	  const crumbs: Crumb[] = [{ label: rootLabel, href: rootHref }]
177	
178	  const segments = path.split('/').filter(Boolean)
179	  // Skip the root segment if it matches the root href (e.g., "admin" when rootHref="/admin")
180	  const rootSegments = rootHref.split('/').filter(Boolean)
181	  const relativeSegments = segments.slice(rootSegments.length)
182	
183	  let built = rootHref
184	  relativeSegments.forEach((seg, i) => {
185	    built += '/' + seg
186	    const isLast = i === relativeSegments.length - 1
187	    const overrideLabel = dynamicLabels[built]
188	    const label =
189	      overrideLabel ??
190	      SEGMENT_LABELS[seg] ??
191	      // Fallback: title-case the segment (swap - → space)
192	      seg.replace(/-/g, ' ').replace(/\b\w/g, (c) => c.toUpperCase())
193	
194	    const isCurrent = isLast && !isTabCrumbPending(path, tab)
195	    const crumb: Crumb = isCurrent ? { label } : { label, href: built }
196	    crumbs.push(crumb)
197	  })
198	
199	  // Append tab crumb if current path is a tab host and tab is set
200	  const tabLabels = TAB_HOSTS[path]
201	  if (tabLabels && tab && tabLabels[tab]) {
202	    crumbs.push({ label: tabLabels[tab] })
203	  }
204	
205	  return crumbs
206	}
207	
208	function isTabCrumbPending(path: string, tab: string | null): boolean {
209	  if (!tab) return false
210	  const tabLabels = TAB_HOSTS[path]
211	  return !!tabLabels && tab in tabLabels
212	}
